metadata.description: High-level component architecture of the Graph Designer Tool as defined in requirement.md and tech-design.md.
Owns the canonical representation of all graph data and its storage lifecycle (tech-design §3.1).
Node / Reference / NodeType / ReferenceType interfaces. UUID v4 identity scheme. Single-root JSON document format with schemaVersion.
Write-through persistence using the native IndexedDB API. Single 'graphs' object store keyed by root Node id. No localStorage fallback.
Read and write root Node documents to the browser's native storage.
Browser-native IndexedDB API. Single source of truth for persisted graph documents; no remote dependency.
Everything the user sees and interacts with visually — canvas, panels, dialogs, forms (tech-design §3.2).
Reads graph documents from the Model Layer to render the canvas and populate panels.
Triggers layout runs, source analysis, AI-assisted edits, and import/export via the Controller Layer.
React Flow (@xyflow/react) canvas. Accessed exclusively through the GraphAdapter contract — application logic never imports React Flow directly.
One GraphAdapter implementation per root node type (document, architecture, code). Share a createGraphCanvas() factory from react-flow-base. Selected from registry by active graph type.
Loads adapter component from ADAPTER_REGISTRY keyed by the active graph type id.
Panels, dialogs, menus, and forms built with shadcn/ui (Radix UI + Tailwind CSS). Raw JSON metadata editing via CodeMirror 6.
Any standard HTTP file server hosting the static bundle (HTML + JS + CSS + assets). No server-side process or configuration required.
Translates user intent into model mutations: layout computation, AI-assisted editing, source analysis, import/export (tech-design §3.3).
Reads and writes graph documents; all mutations are written through to IndexedDB.
Invokes per-type source analyzers via ANALYZER_REGISTRY.
Pure functions (root: Node, params) => Map<id, {x,y}>. Strategies: hierarchical (Dagre), force-directed (d3-force), radial (in-house), grid (in-house). No side effects on the model.
Minimal OpenAI-compatible HTTP client. Generates patches for node/reference label, type, and metadata only — no structural mutations. Feature-flagged (ai.enabled, off by default).
Single generatePatchForNodeOrReference call. Only executed when ai.enabled flag is on and provider is reachable.
OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. Optional — all authoring workflows are fully functional without it. Configured via a single endpoint setting.
Coordinates per-type analyzers. Each analyzer is a pure async function: (source: string) => root Node. The draft is returned to the user for review; it is persisted only on confirmation.
Extracts Markdown heading structure into a section-node hierarchy using a no-dependency regex parser. Falls back to AI Editing Client for unstructured plain text when ai.enabled is on.
AI-assisted section detection for plain-text input without heading structure. Only when ai.enabled.
TypeScript / JavaScript: TypeScript Compiler API walks the AST in memory (no emit). Python / Java / C#: pattern-based extraction at reduced fidelity. No AI involvement.
Straight passthrough. Validates an uploaded JSON file against the graph document format and returns it directly as the draft root Node. No parsing, inference, or AI required (MVP simplification).
Lossless serialisation and deserialisation of root Node documents to and from the canonical open JSON format. No information is lost across a round-trip.
Isolated modules under src/graph-types/{type}/. Each module owns its NodeType, metadata schemas, adapter, and analyzer. Assembled by a central registry (tech-design §3.4).
NODE_TYPES + ADAPTER_REGISTRY + ANALYZER_REGISTRY. The only file outside a graph-type module that imports from all three modules. Exports the full catalog to the rest of the application.
node-type (root, section), metadata-schema, React Flow adapter, and heading-based Markdown analyzer for document graphs.
node-type (InternalComponent, ExternalComponent), metadata-schema (componentKind, exposes), React Flow adapter, and JSON-passthrough analyzer for architecture graphs.
node-type (package, class, interface, member), metadata-schema, React Flow adapter, and TypeScript Compiler API-based analyzer for code graphs.
